cards.explanation: The answer is one of these little ones. Jesus says it would be better for the person to have a millstone hung around his neck and be thrown into the sea "…than to cause one of these little ones to stumble." (Luke 17:2) That's a heavy line, so I'll say it plainly and leave it alone. He doesn't tell us here who the little ones are, so I won't guess either.

The answer is forgive, friends. Jesus puts it in two short steps: "If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him." (Luke 17:3) Notice the order. The rebuke comes first, and the forgiveness follows when he repents.

The answer is seven times, bakers. Jesus says, "Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him." (Luke 17:4) Seven times in one day. That's a lot of tally marks on the oven door, and Jesus still says forgive.

The answer is "Increase our faith." The apostles said to the Lord, "Increase our faith!" (Luke 17:5) The text doesn't say why they asked, but I think that forgiveness talk landed hard. I'd have asked for more of something too.

The answer is faith the size of a mustard seed, friends. Jesus says, "If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you." (Luke 17:6) A mustard seed is tiny. Jesus picked it, so I'm not going to argue with Him.

The answer is False. In Jesus' picture, the servant doesn't pull up a chair yet. The master says, "Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink, and afterward you may eat and drink…" (Luke 17:8) The servant does get his meal, bakers, but afterward, and that order is how Jesus sets it up.

The answer is serve! The master says, "Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink…" (Luke 17:8) Notice the order, friends. Dress yourself first, like me tying on my apron before anybody touches a cookie, then serve. The servant's own turn to eat comes afterward.

The answer is that the servant only did his job, friends. Jesus asks, "Does he thank the servant because he did what he was told?" (Luke 17:9) It's a question, and the picture gives its answer. Then verse 10 ends with "we have only done our duty."

The answer is "We are unworthy servants." Jesus says, "So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’…" (Luke 17:10) It's a humble line, bakers. The servant picture from verses 7 to 9 leads right to it.
